extracted.intended_audience: students and readers learning complex analysis (advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter on Cauchy's theorem and its applications in complex analysis, presenting Goursat's theorem, Cauchy integral formulas, consequences (Liouville, fundamental theorem of algebra), and related results and techniques (Morera, uniform limits, Schwarz reflection, contour-deformation examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goursat's theorem (triangle integral zero)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is an open set in C, and T ⊂ Ω a triangle whose interior is also contained in Ω, then whenever f is holomorphic in Ω, ∮_T f(z) dz = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via successive bisection of the triangle producing nested triangles whose diameter → 0; expand f near the common limiting point z0 as f(z)=f(z0)+f'(z0)(z−z0)+ψ(z)(z−z0) with ψ→0 and estimate integrals to conclude limit 0. This is the starting point from which most subsequent results are deduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy's theorem for rectangles (corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set Ω that contains a rectangle R and its interior, then ∮_R f(z) dz = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consequence of Goursat's theorem by splitting the rectangle into two triangles (orientations chosen consistently) and using cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local existence of primitives in a disc
rubrics_metrics.description: A holomorphic function in an open disc has a primitive in that disc (Theorem 2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the primitive by integrating f along polygonal paths γ_z from a basepoint (0) to z consisting of horizontal then vertical segments; show independence of path using Goursat for triangles/rectangles and then compute derivative of the constructed F to get F'(z)=f(z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy's theorem in a disc (closed-curve integrals vanish)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in a disc, then ∮_γ f(z) dz = 0 for any closed curve γ in that disc (Theorem 2.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from existence of a primitive on the disc; applies whenever an 'interior' can be unambiguously defined and polygonal constructions (as in Theorem 2.1) are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toy contour definition and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'toy contour' is any closed curve where the notion of interior is obvious, and a construction similar to the polygonal-path argument in Theorem 2.1 is possible in a neighborhood of the curve and its interior; positive orientation is interior to the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: circles, triangles, rectangles, keyhole contours, semicircles, indented semicircles, sectors, parallelograms, rectangular/multiple keyholes. For any toy contour γ, if f is holomorphic in an open set containing γ and its interior then ∮_γ f(z) dz = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contour-deformation / shifting technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrals over lines (e.g., the real axis) can be shifted in the complex plane using Cauchy's theorem when the integrand is holomorphic (or suitably decaying) in the strip/region between the original and shifted contour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Example 1: shifting the real-line integral upward/downward for entire decaying integrands (e.g., e^{-πz^2}) and justifying vanishing contributions of vertical sides by exponential decay estimates. Ensure conditions that integrals over added sides go to zero as |Re(z)|→∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy integral formula (representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set that contains the closure of a disc D and C is its positively oriented boundary, then for any z∈D, f(z) = (1/2πi) ∮_C f(ζ)/(ζ−z) dζ (Theorem 4.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved using a keyhole contour around z to exclude the singularity, letting corridor width → 0 and small circle radius → 0; decompose integrand as (f(ζ)−f(z))/(ζ−z) + f(z)/(ζ−z) and note boundedness of first term's integral and explicit evaluation of the second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy formulas for derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set Ω and C is a circle in Ω whose interior is contained in Ω, then for z in interior of C, f^{(n)}(z) = n!/(2πi) ∮_C f(ζ)/(ζ−z)^{n+1} dζ (Corollary 4.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by induction differentiating the integral formula and estimating difference quotients; ensures holomorphic functions have derivatives of all orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy inequalities (derivative bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set containing closure of disc D centered at z0 of radius R, then |f^{(n)}(z0)| ≤ n! (sup_{ζ∈C} |f(ζ)|) / R^n (Corollary 4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the derivative Cauchy formula and estimate integrals over the circle using sup norm on boundary; useful for bounding growth of derivatives and proofs like Liouville.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power series expansion of holomorphic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set Ω and D is a disc centered at z0 whose closure is contained in Ω, then f has a power series expansion f(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞ a_n (z−z0)^n for all z∈D with a_n = f^{(n)}(z0)/n! (Theorem 4.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cauchy integral formula and geometric series expansion 1/(ζ−z) = 1/(ζ−z0) · 1/[1−(z−z0)/(ζ−z0)], justify uniform convergence on boundary to interchange sum and integral; shows holomorphic ⇒ analytic (local power series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liouville's theorem (bounded entire functions are constant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is entire and bounded, then f is constant (Corollary 4.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Cauchy inequalities |f^{(n)}(z0)| ≤ n! B / R^n; letting R→∞ forces derivatives to vanish; used in applications like the fundamental theorem of algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental theorem of algebra via complex analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Every non-constant polynomial P(z)=a_n z^n + ... + a_0 has a root in C (Corollary 4.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If P had no roots then 1/P is entire and bounded (show |P(z)| ≥ c|z|^n for large |z| and bounded away from 0 on compact disc), contradicting Liouville; hence polynomial must have a root.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeros accumulation ⇒ identically zero (identity theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in a region Ω and vanishes on a sequence of distinct points with a limit point in Ω, then f is identically 0 (Theorem 4.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand f in power series around limit point; if not identically zero the lowest nonzero coefficient yields contradiction; then use connectedness to extend vanishing to whole region. Corollary: analytic continuation is unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of analytic continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: If f and g are holomorphic in a region Ω and agree on some non-empty open subset (or a sequence with an accumulation point in Ω), then they agree throughout Ω (Corollary 4.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consequence of identity theorem (zeros of f−g accumulate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morera's theorem (converse of Cauchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is continuous on an open disc D and for any triangle T contained in D we have ∮_T f(z) dz = 0, then f is holomorphic (Theorem 5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a primitive using the same polygonal-path method as in existence theorem; then by regularity the primitive is differentiable and its derivative equals f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform limit theorem for holomorphic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If {f_n} is a sequence of holomorphic functions that converges uniformly to f on every compact subset of Ω, then f is holomorphic in Ω (Theorem 5.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: for any disc D with closure in Ω, triangle integrals for f_n vanish; uniform convergence allows passing limit inside integral to get ∮_T f = 0, apply Morera. Use for constructing holomorphic limits like series or Riemann-sum integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform convergence of derivatives under compact-uniform convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Under hypotheses of uniform convergence on compact subsets of Ω of holomorphic functions f_n→f, the derivatives f_n^{(k)} converge uniformly to f^{(k)} on every compact subset of Ω (Theorem 5.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cauchy integral bounds on smaller discs inside Ω to control derivatives; inequality sup_{z∈Ω_δ} |F'(z)| ≤ (1/δ) sup_{ζ∈Ω} |F(ζ)| (and higher-order analogues) gives uniform control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic functions defined by parameter integrals (sufficient conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F(z,s) is defined on Ω×[0,1] with (i) F(·,s) holomorphic for each s and (ii) F continuous on Ω×[0,1], then f(z)=∫_0^1 F(z,s) ds is holomorphic on Ω (Theorem 5.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint continuity ensures uniform continuity on compact z-sets; approximate integral by Riemann sums of holomorphic functions which converge uniformly on compacts to f, then apply uniform limit theorem (Theorem 5.2) or Morera to conclude holomorphicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry principle (gluing across real axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Ω symmetric with respect to the real line with Ω+ (upper) and Ω− (lower) and I = Ω∩R. If f+ and f− are holomorphic in Ω+ and Ω− respectively, extend continuously to I, and satisfy f+(x)=f−(x) for all x∈I, then the glued function f defined by f=f+ on Ω+, f=f− on Ω−, and equal on I is holomorphic on all of Ω (Theorem 5.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Morera's theorem: for triangles intersecting I raise/lower edges slightly to apply holomorphicity in upper/lower parts and let perturbation →0; split triangles if interior crosses I. Continuity on I plus matching values allows holomorphic extension across I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schwarz reflection principle (real boundary reflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in Ω+ (upper half region), extends continuously to I, and is real-valued on I, then there exists F holomorphic in all of Ω (symmetric region) such that F=f on Ω+ (Theorem 5.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define extension F(z) for z∈Ω− by F(z)=overline{f( ar z)} (or equivalently f reflected); the symmetry principle ensures holomorphicity if the reflected values match on I and continuity holds. Power series arguments near points of Ω− show series coefficients are conjugates and produce holomorphic extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toy-contour based evaluation techniques (examples catalog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various specially-shaped toy contours (keyhole, rectangular keyhole, multiple keyhole, semicircle, indented semicircle, sector, parallelogram) are standardly used to evaluate integrals via residues/Cauchy theorem and contour deformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select contour shape appropriate to integrand's singularities and branch cuts; justify limits (small indent radius →0 or large radius →∞) via estimates; use decomposition into parts where Cauchy's theorem applies to reduce or compute real integrals.
